\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{غرور} (ghurūr)}{غرور (ghurūr)}]{\ur{غرور} (ghurūr) — arrogance; conceit}

\label{lesson:UR-C452-ghurur}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for contrite, then the Urdu for embarrassment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{غرور}}
\textbf{\ur{غرور}} — \emph{ghurūr} — \textquotedblleft{}arrogance; conceit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اسے} \ur{اپنی} \ur{طاقت} \ur{پر} \ur{غرور} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{use apnī tāqat par ghurūr hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He is conceited about his strength.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{غرور}} (\emph{ghurūr}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ghurūr}, \textquotedblleft{}self-delusion, vanity\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghurūr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghurūr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{use apnī tāqat par ghurūr hai.} — He is conceited about his strength.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for contrite, then the Urdu for embarrassment, then say \emph{ghurūr} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اترانا} (itrānā)}{اترانا (itrānā)}]{\ur{اترانا} (itrānā) — to put on airs; to strut}

\label{lesson:UR-C452-itrana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for arrogance, then the Urdu for boasting.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اترانا}}
\textbf{\ur{اترانا}} — \emph{itrānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to put on airs; to strut\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{نئے} \ur{کپڑے} \ur{پہن} \ur{کر} \ur{وہ} \ur{اترا} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{naye kapṛe pahan kar voh itrā rahī thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She was strutting about in her new clothes.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{اترایا}, \emph{voh itrāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اترانا}} (\emph{itrānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{itrānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to strut\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{itvará}, \textquotedblleft{}walking\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1566).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نخرا} (nakhrā)}{نخرا (nakhrā)}]{\ur{نخرا} (nakhrā) — fussiness; airs and graces}

\label{lesson:UR-C452-nakhra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for boasting, then the Urdu for to put on airs.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نخرا}}
\textbf{\ur{نخرا}} — \emph{nakhrā} — \textquotedblleft{}fussiness; airs and graces\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{بچہ} \ur{کھانے} \ur{میں} \ur{بڑے} \ur{نخرے} \ur{کرتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih bachchā khāne meṅ baṛe nakhre kartā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\textbf{\ur{نخرا}} (\emph{nakhrā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{nakhra}, \textquotedblleft{}coquetry, airs\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تکبر} (takabbur)}{تکبر (takabbur)}]{\ur{تکبر} (takabbur) — haughtiness}

\label{lesson:UR-C452-takabbur}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to put on airs, then the Urdu for fussiness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تکبر}}
\textbf{\ur{تکبر}} — \emph{takabbur} — \textquotedblleft{}haughtiness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{تکبر} \ur{انسان} \ur{کو} \ur{چھوٹا} \ur{بنا} \ur{دیتا} \ur{ہے۔}
